title: Local base publication with compare-and-swap, rollback, and recovery commands
description:
Phase 4 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign.

Create scripts/basePublication.ts: publish only after the root integration OID exists. Revalidate all recorded base OIDs and every approval input first, then update one canonical local base ref per logical repository using compare-and-swap semantics, and align other local occurrences' base branches through local fetch and fast-forward. If any update fails, roll back the already-updated refs to their recorded OIDs. If publication or rollback is incomplete, preserve the integration and recovery refs and report exact recovery commands.

Rollback must not stop at the first failure in a way that leaves advanced repositories without recovery instructions — every repository's state and its recovery command must be reported.

Tests: a base ref that moved since approval blocks publication entirely; compare-and-swap prevents clobbering a concurrent update; a mid-sequence failure rolls back every already-updated ref to its recorded OID; a failing rollback preserves integration and recovery refs and reports an exact command per affected repository; other occurrences fast-forward locally without a remote push; nothing publishes before the root integration OID exists.

title: Archive only successfully published tasks
description:
Phase 4 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign.

Create scripts/taskArchival.ts: return task-level merge results after successful publication and archive only the explicit task numbers whose integration was successfully published. The whole-run approval already authorizes finalization and archival, so no second post-merge approval is introduced.

A task in a conflicted, skipped, rolled-back, or partially published repository is never archived, and archival must be driven by an explicit list rather than by inferring success from the absence of errors.

Tests: a run where one logical repository rolled back archives none of that repository's tasks while archiving the successfully published ones; conflicted and skipped tasks stay open in tasks.json; archival requires the explicit published list; no second approval prompt is issued; archived entries land in completedTasks.json with their commit hashes.

title: Production cutover to the recursive repository workflow
description:
Phase 4 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign — the cutover that finally routes production through everything built in Phases 1 to 3.

Replace the flat-path helpers with their graph-based equivalents at their call sites: scripts/repositoryBranches.ts (collectRepositorySources, submodulePaths, createBranchInEveryRepository), scripts/taskGroups.ts (grouping now via scripts/canonicalTaskGroups.ts), scripts/prepareTasks.ts (discovery, worktree and branch creation, workflow arguments), and scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts (finalization and publication via scripts/runFinalizer.ts, scripts/runConsolidation.ts, scripts/operationPush.ts, scripts/basePublication.ts, scripts/taskArchival.ts). Rewire skills/tackle-tasks/tackle-tasks.workflow.js and skills/tackle-tasks/SKILL.md so preparation returns recursive graph metadata, hook mode, recovery refs, test receipts, review handoffs, and readyForApproval instead of immediate merge results, and so the approval gate runs before finalization.

Activate the new manifest/workflow version only after the complete end-to-end suite passes. Preserve legacy worktrees and route legacy manifests through scripts/legacyManifest.ts to their existing compatible tooling or a non-destructive refusal.

Tests: existing prepareTasks and mergeTaskWorktrees suites are updated to the new interfaces and pass; the workflow returns readyForApproval rather than merge results before approval; a legacy manifest is refused non-destructively with recovery instructions and its worktrees survive; the version flips only when the full suite is green.

title: RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture and Phase 4 acceptance run
description:
Phase 4 of the recursive repository-discovery redesign — the final acceptance gate.

Build a RevEng-shaped end-to-end fixture in tests/fixtures/revengGraph.ts containing tmux_lib at tmux_lib, jfred/external/tmux_lib, and jfred/jfredToolsPlugin/external/tmux_lib; two occurrences each of claude_plugin_lib and scenarios; nested submodules beneath ordinary directories; and distinct parent chains. Drive a full run against it in tests/revengEndToEnd.test.ts.

Verify in that fixture that a change originating from any repeated occurrence converges everywhere; all child and ancestor suites pass; approval precedes every commit, merge, and push; all occurrence histories consolidate into one operation per logical repository; gitlinks propagate through the correct explicit parents to the root; and every intended local base ends at the expected merge commit. Also verify no semantic commit, push, integration merge, base mutation, or archival occurs before approval, and that only successfully published tasks are archived.

Phase 4 acceptance: the recursive workflow is the production path, completes the RevEng-shaped run without data loss, and archives only tasks whose integration was successfully published.

title: new skill: /tackle-unblocked-tasks
description:
Works by finding all tasks with empty blockedBy[] arrays, returning an array of task numbers as `unblockedTaskNumbers` sorted lowest to highest, then executes the same code path that invoking 'tackle-tasks unblockedTaskNumbers valid' uses.  

Add an exported `unblockedTaskNumbers(openTasks)` helper to scripts/taskFiles.ts returning ascending-sorted task numbers with empty blockedBy[] arrays.

title: tackle-tasks-loop skill
description:
another mode that keeps checking the tasks.json for blockers on a timer,tackles them, then does unblocked until the whole list is completed.  End result of this script-loop running is that the user just has to run it once, then just use 'create-task' or 'goal-tasks' to define what to build, and the background agents build everything that has a task created. 

Create skills/tackle-tasks-loop/SKILL.md only — skills are auto-discovered by directory, so no plugin.json or marketplace.json registration is needed. The skill wraps the existing global `/loop` skill to invoke `taskTools:tackle-tasks unblocked` (task 37's mode) on an interval. Use scripts/taskStats.ts for the stop condition: end when the open count reaches 0, and bail out when a full pass finds nothing unblocked so it does not spin on a fully blocked backlog. No new TypeScript and no new test file — checkBlockers.ts --unblocked and taskStats.ts already supply every count this needs.

title: merge-worktree-tasks skill
description:
a way to check if worktrees weren't merged and if there are open tasks that haven't been completed and are assigned to those worktrees, and then to run the merge-worktrees script to merge them *if the task is approved*.  Cause: sometimes I forget to commit when tasks are completed, which blocks the worktrees from being commited. 

Worktrees live at `tmpdir()/taskTools-wt/<basename(repoRoot)>/group-<groupId>` on branch `task-group-<groupId>`, but groupId is recomputed every prepareTasks run and never persisted, so a leftover worktree cannot be matched to task numbers by groupId. Match by file overlap instead: read the worktree branch's changed files plus its uncommitted status and compare them against `declaredFiles(task)` from scripts/taskGroups.ts for open tasks.

Extend scripts/mergeTaskWorktrees.ts rather than adding a new script: add `listTaskWorktrees(repoRoot)` (parse `git worktree list --porcelain`, keep only paths matching the taskTools-wt convention), `findUnmergedTaskWorktrees(repoRoot, sourceBranch, openTasks)` (unmerged-commit count plus uncommitted status, changed files matched to declared files), and CLI modes `--discover` and `--merge <worktree>` reusing the existing collectRepositorySources, currentBranchName, mergeGroupBranchIntoRepo and removeWorktreeAndBranch. Create skills/merge-worktree-tasks/SKILL.md: run --discover, report each unmerged worktree with its matched open task numbers, gate the merge behind explicit user approval via AskUserQuestion, then run --merge only for approved worktrees.

title: add 'verify plan' and 'test' to tackle-tasks workflow
description:
the workflow does plan -> implement -> typecheck -> merge. it needs to add 'verify' after plan, and then 'test' after 'implement'.  'verify' is a separate agent that checks if the plan is good or not.  'test' is running the tests for the files touched by the implementation, and then reporting the test results to the implementing agent to fix or not.

In skills/tackle-tasks/tackle-tasks.workflow.js add a Verify phase (one agent per task after Plan, gating which planned tasks reach Implement) and a Test phase (one agent per group after Implement, feeding failures back into runWorker the way the existing partial-requeue loop does). Both need meta.phases entries, result arrays threaded into the final return, and an extra pipeline() stage.

The file is 194 of the 250-line cap and the two phases add roughly 60-100 lines, so split first: move VERIFY_SCHEMA, TEST_SCHEMA and the verifierBrief/testerBrief prompt builders (plus the existing plannerBrief/workerBrief for consistency) into a new skills/tackle-tasks/tackle-tasks.briefs.js imported by the workflow, leaving the workflow as thin orchestration wiring. The Test agent brief should point at the existing scripts/relatedTests.ts discovery pattern rather than duplicating test discovery; relatedTests.ts and testPolicy.ts themselves need no changes.

title: Rewrite pick-a-task's selection criteria to use the difficulty field
description:
Revisit how pick-a-task chooses tasks once the `difficulty` field is supported on tasks.json entries.

Today skills/pick-a-task/SKILL.md picks the N easiest open tasks by having the agent read every task and reason in prose about which are simplest, comparing each against the current state of the project. Once each task carries a difficulty rating (1-5), most of that reasoning becomes a sort: filter to unblocked, order by difficulty ascending, take N.

Rewrite the picking criteria to use the field, and decide what judgment is still worth spending prose on. The remaining candidate is the relevance check — is this task still needed given the current codebase? — which is separate from difficulty and cannot be sorted.

Blocked by the task that adds the difficulty field to tasks.json entries and to skills/create-task/template/taskTemplate.json; that task does not exist yet, so add its number to blockedBy once it is created.
